# INSTITUTIONAL EQUITY UNDERWRITING MEMORANDUM
## Accelerant Holdings (NYSE: ARX) — Pending Take-Private by Thoma Bravo

> **DECISIVE FACT (established via web research, outranks the data pack's standalone framing):** On **August 13, 2026**, Accelerant entered a **definitive agreement to be acquired by Thoma Bravo in an all-cash transaction at $20.25 per share** (Class A and Class B), enterprise value >$4B, **no financing condition** (Thoma Bravo equity-committed), expected to close **H1 2027**, outside date **Aug 13, 2027 (extendable to Nov 13, 2027 if only insurance-regulatory conditions remain)**, with a **6% p.a. ticking fee ($0.00333/share/day)** accruing if insurance regulatory approvals delay closing. **Altamont Capital Partners holds ~82% of voting rights and has pre-committed to vote in favor.** The Special Committee and Board approved unanimously. **T0 = $19.835 is a ~2.1% discount to the contractual $20.25.** This is therefore a **merger-arbitrage / deal-completion underwriting**, not a standalone fundamental buy. All standalone analysis below serves only to (a) justify the deal price and (b) anchor the deal-break (bear) floor.

---

## SECTION 0 — Analysis Overview

| Field | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Ticker / Company | ARX — Accelerant Holdings Ltd (Cayman) | [Actual] |
| Exchange | NYSE | [Actual] |
| Price T0 | **$19.835** (2026-09-10) | [Aggregator] |
| 52-Wk Range | $9.18 – $20.51 | [Aggregator] |
| Deal Price (contractual) | **$20.25 / share cash** | [Actual] |
| Deal Premium to T0 | +2.09% | [Arithmetic] |
| Deal Premium to pre-ann. close (Aug 12 ≈ $13.59) | +49% | [Actual] |
| Shares (vendor, Class A+B) | 217.19M (MarketWatch shows 112.8M Class A only — per-share math unaffected) | [Aggregator] |
| Market Cap (at T0) | ~$4.31B | [Aggregator] |

**Business Value Decomposition (Pillar 1):**
1. **Transactional / Underwriting Deliveries** — Accelerant-retained exchange premium (~10–13% of EWP) written through its own fronting structure; cyclical, loss-ratio-exposed (~52% gross loss ratio), capital-intensive. *Small and de-emphasized.*
2. **Captive Installed-Base / Recurring Fee Annuity (the core asset)** — the **Accelerant Risk Exchange**: fee-based, capital-light revenue charged on **Exchange Written Premium (EWP)**. TTM EWP = **$4.59B** (Jun-30-2026), 3rd-party (capital-light) penetration rising 16%→47% YoY, **Net Revenue Retention 111–157%**, fee-based EBITDA margin ~30%. This is the compounding "installed base" that Thoma Bravo is buying.
3. **Strategic Optionality** — AI underwriting (ARC data agent), 22 countries / ~700 products, MGA network (314 members), and Thoma Bravo's post-close platforming capital.

**Headline Valuation Summary (deal-completion framing):**

| Case | IV | Prob | Driver |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Base** | **$20.25** | 80% | Deal closes on schedule, no ticking |
| **Bull** | **$20.55** | 15% | Deal closes after regulatory delay → ~3 mo ticking fee |
| **Bear** | **$13.00** | 5% | Deal terminates → reverts to governance-discounted standalone |
| **Expected IV** | **$19.93** | 100% | Prob-weighted |
| **MoS vs T0** | **+0.48%** | — | Thin (fairly-priced carry) |

**Data Tier confidence:** Deal terms = **Tier 1 (company/buyer filings & press releases)**. Standalone financials = **Tier 2 (company press releases; pack SEC extract is distorted by the one-time IPO profits-interest charge)**. Regulatory investigation = **Tier 4 [Unconfirmed]**.

---

## SECTION 1 — Macro Context & Regime Alignment

- **10Y Rf = 4.83%** [verified anchor, 2026-09-09]; 10Y-2Y +0.39% (steepening); BAA spread 1.55%; HY OAS 2.71%; Regime = **Reflation**.
- **Enterprise sensitivity to macro: LOW.** This is the defining feature of the position. The $20.25 contract is **financing-free** (Thoma Bravo equity-committed), so the trade is **decoupled from the credit cycle, rate path, and equity beta**. A +100–200 bps WACC shock does not impair the deal price; it only marginally affects the (irrelevant-to-the-trade) standalone DCF. The only macro-adjacent risk is a systemic credit event that could pressure a PE sponsor's balance sheet — low probability, and Thoma Bravo's $172B AUM / committed equity makes it a non-issue.
- **Implication:** Macro is a non-driver. Conviction is set by **deal-completion probability**, not regime.

---

## SECTION 1.5 — Historical Base Rates

- **Take-private completion base rate (no financing condition + majority pre-commit):** ~93–97%. The absence of a financing condition removes the single largest historical break cause; an 82% pre-committed vote removes shareholder-vote risk.
- **Take-private premium base rate:** 30–60% for high-quality, growing assets. The 49% premium sits mid-range — consistent with a well-negotiated, board-recommended deal (Morgan Stanley + Houlihan Lokey process), not a distressed fire-sale.
- **Insurance change-of-control regulatory approval:** Typically a notification/approval process, not a veto; hard rejections of a change-of-control are rare. Delay (not block) is the modal adverse outcome — which is exactly what the **ticking fee** was engineered to absorb.
- **MGA / specialty-insurance platform EBITDA multiple base rate:** 10–20x (Acrisure, AssuredPartners, BroadStreet-type comps). A ~14x fee-EBITDA standalone multiple is the anchor for the bear floor.
- **Model deviation justification:** I do **not** apply a Gordon-growth GDP clamp to the standalone terminal; the fee annuity has secular growth (3rd-party penetration, MGA consolidation) supporting a 4–5% terminal g. This is used only to confirm the deal price exceeds standalone (supporting completion) and to floor the bear.

---

## SECTION 2 — Business Quality & Competitive Moat

**Business in 3 sentences:** Accelerant operates a two-sided "Accelerant Risk Exchange" that connects specialty-insurance MGAs (risk sellers) with risk-capital partners (insurers/reinsurers), charging fees on the premium that flows through the platform. It is rapidly shifting from capital-intensive retained underwriting to a **capital-light, fee-based model** (3rd-party penetration 16%→47% YoY), with TTM EWP of $4.59B and ~30% fee-based EBITDA margins. The moat is proprietary risk data + AI underwriting + network effects, but the structure carries a **related-party / governance overhang** (Altamont-linked fronting carrier Hadron ~60% of 3rd-party premium; Altamont-linked reinsurance broker Augment Risk) that is under **reported [Unconfirmed]** regulatory scrutiny.

**7-Factor Moat Score (0–3 each):**

| Factor | Score | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Data / Analytics | 3 | Proprietary specialty-risk dataset, AI/ARC underwriting, compounding with each placement |
| Network effects | 3 | Two-sided: more MGAs + more capital → better pricing → more members |
| Switching costs | 2 | Data history + integration, but capital partners can exit a cycle |
| Brand / Trust | 2 | Specialty trust, but governance overhang discounts it |
| Scale / Cost | 2 | Capital-light, but small vs. incumbent MGAs/brokers |
| Regulatory / Licensing | 2 | 22 countries / ~700 products is an asset **and** the source of the regulatory risk |
| Installed base / Recurring | 3 | EWP $4.59B TTM, NRR >100%, compounding fleet |
| **Total** | **17 / 21** | → **4.3 / 5.0** (reported **4.0** after netting the active regulatory narrowing) |

**Moat Direction:** **Widening** (data + 3rd-party penetration) **but offset by related-party regulatory scrutiny** (Lloyd's "alignment of interest" concerns on a prior syndicate; reported DoI probe). Net: **Stable-to-Widening with a governance hair.**

**Lynch Classification:** **Special Situation — pending take-private** (not a classic Lynch growth/compounder while the deal is pending; the standalone would be a "Specialty/Growth" name).

**Financial Strength scorecard:** Cash $1.799B vs LT debt $0.121B → **net cash ~$1.68B** [Filed]. Equity $0.698B, retained earnings -$1.537B (distorted by the one-time IPO profits-interest charge, not operating). Balance sheet is **fortress for the trade** — the company cannot fail to fund a deal it is being bought out of, and the buyer is equity-committed.

---

## SECTION 2.5 — Adjusted Financials & Lifecycle Economics

**The GAAP loss is an accounting artifact, not economic reality.** FY2025 GAAP net loss of **-$1,345M** is driven by a **$1,380M non-cash, equity-neutral "profits interest distribution expense"** from the IPO settlement (fully offset by a corresponding capital contribution from Accelerant Holdings LP). It is **not** an impairment and **not** an operating loss. [Actual — company reconciliation]

| Metric (company-reported) | FY2024 | FY2025 | Q1-26 | Q2-26 | H1-26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $602.6M | $912.9M | $273.3M | $356.9M | $630.2M |
| EWP | $3,108M | $4,191M | $1,139M | $1,322M | $2,461M |
| 3rd-party % of EWP | 16% | 30% | 41% | 47% | 44% |
| Adj EBITDA | $113M | $281.8M | $66.1M | $93.1M | $159.2M |
| Adj EBITDA margin | 19% | 31% | 24% | 31% | 28% |
| Adj net income | $66.7M | $178.7M | $37.7M | $70.0M | $107.7M |
| Adj EPS (dil) | — | ~$0.80 | $0.17 | $0.32 | $0.49 |
| GAAP net income | $22.9M | **-$1,345M** | -$4.1M | $80.0M | $75.9M |
| Gross loss ratio | 54.3% | 51.3% | 52.1% | 52.0% | 52.0% |

**SBC treatment:** FY2025 SBC = $54M (per company reconciliation; pack filed series $43M — use the larger, more complete figure). SBC is a real economic expense but is immaterial to the trade (the deal price is fixed).

**Complete Value Cycle:** EWP is the locked-in "installed base." NRR of 111–157% means the premium fleet is **compounding, not churning** — each dollar of EWP is a recurring fee annuity. 3rd-party penetration rising to 47% means the annuity is becoming **capital-lighter and higher-margin** over time. This is the asset Thoma Bravo underwrote at >$4B EV; it confirms the deal price is **above** a governance-discounted standalone, which is the single strongest completion signal.

**Normalized Owner Earnings (standalone, context only):** Fee-based EBITDA ~$276M (FY26 guide) → after SBC, D&A, tax, and a modest reinvestment for a capital-light platform, normalized owner earnings ≈ $180–220M. At ~217M shares, that's ~$0.85–1.00/share normalized — the standalone is a **multiple** play, not an earnings-yield play, and the 49% deal premium is what makes it rational.

---

## SECTION 3 — Valuation Synthesis & Triangulation

**Primary valuation = the contractual deal price, $20.25.** Triangulated three ways:

**(a) Deal-price anchor [Actual]:** $20.25 cash, financing-free, 82% pre-commit, unanimous board. This is the operative "intrinsic value" for the position.

**(b) Standalone DCF / cap-rate cross-check [Estimate]:**
- WACC (standalone, context only): Rf 4.83% + 5.0% ERP × ~1.2β + ~1% size/governance = **~11.5–12%**.
- Terminal g = **4.5%** (secular MGA/specialty growth; **not** clamped to 3.5% GDP). Net cap rate = 11.8% − 4.5% = 7.3% → **~13.7x terminal multiple**.
- Fee EBITDA path: 2026E $276M → 2030E ~$540M (decelerating 25%→12%). PV of explicit EBITDA ≈ $1.4B; PV of terminal ≈ $4.4B → fee EV ≈ $5.8B **before** governance discount.
- **Governance/related-party discount of 25–40%** (DoI probe [Unconfirmed], Lloyd's concerns, 82% insider control, thin float) brings standalone equity to **~$13–16/share** — consistent with the **$13.59 pre-announcement close**.
- **Conclusion:** Deal price ($20.25) **exceeds** the governance-discounted standalone ($13–16). A rational board sells above standalone; this is why the deal is likely to close and why the bear floor is ~$13.

**(c) Reverse-DCF / market-implied completion probability:** T0 $19.835 is a **2.09% discount** to $20.25. Decomposing the discount: break-risk × downside (~$6.8 to $13.4) + small carry/time cost (~$0.15). Solving: break-risk ≈ **3.9%**, i.e., the market implies **~96% completion**. My independent estimate is **95%** (slightly more conservative, reflecting the unconfirmed regulatory overhang). **The trade is roughly fairly priced** — my expected IV ($19.93) ≈ T0 ($19.835).

**WACC derivation note:** Because the position is a financing-free cash contract, WACC is **not** the decision variable; it is shown only to floor the standalone bear.

---

## SECTION 3.5 — Second-Order Effects & Reflexivity

- **Competitive counter-moves:** A terminated deal would likely **attract a superior/competing bid** (the 49% premium signals the board will re-shop; the business is genuinely attractive). This is a **reflexive floor** under the bear — a break is more likely to re-rate the stock *up* toward a new bid than to collapse it, though a break *caused by a regulatory finding* would suppress it.
- **Pricing tolerance / elasticity:** The ticking fee makes the seller's reservation price **rise with time** (6% p.a.), so there is **no seller incentive to walk** over a delay — a structural completion tailwind.
- **Balance-sheet reflexivity:** Net cash ~$1.68B + buyer equity commitment = no leverage spiral risk. The 82% Altamont block + founder rollover means the insider base is **aligned with completion**, not exit.
- **Regulatory reflexivity:** A *negative* DoI finding would be a double hit (deal risk + standalone governance discount). A *clean* finding removes the overhang and would push standalone value up, further supporting completion.

---

## SECTION 4 — Scenarios & Bounded Distributions

Causal stress-test (bottom-up): the "shock" is **deal termination**, transmitted via (i) a hard insurance-regulatory rejection of the related-party structure, or (ii) a failed shareholder vote (near-impossible at 82% pre-commit). There is **no financing leg to fail** and **no volume/margin de-leverage** in the trade itself — the contract is fixed. The standalone operating engine (EWP annuity) is **not** stressed in the bear because the bear is a *deal* outcome, not an *operating* outcome; the EWP fleet (NRR >100%) would continue to compound under any owner, which is what keeps the bear at ~$13 rather than a collapse.

| Scenario | Prob | Intrinsic Value | Causal Path |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Base** | 80% | **$20.25** | Deal closes H1 2027 on schedule; no ticking; shareholder vote + regulatory clearance. |
| **Bull** | 15% | **$20.55** | Deal closes but insurance regulatory approval delays past the Ticking Start Date → ~3 months × $0.00333/day ≈ +$0.30. (A competing top-up bid is a low-prob tail folded in qualitatively, not added.) |
| **Bear** | 5% | **$13.00** | Deal terminates (definitive adverse insurance-regulatory determination or termination right invoked) → stock reverts to governance-discounted standalone (~$13–14 pre-deal level, hair for a negative-catalyst break). |
| **Expected IV** | 100% | **$19.93** | 0.80×20.25 + 0.15×20.55 + 0.05×13.00 |

**Confidence Intervals:**
- **50% CI:** $20.25 – $20.55 (deal completes, the 95% probability mass).
- **80% CI (practical bounds):** $13.00 – $20.55 (full support, dominated by the base case).
- The distribution is **degenerate-high**: 80% of mass at $20.25, with a single 5% left tail at $13.00.

**Contracted Visibility Floor:** N/A in the operating sense (no backlog/ARR floor to breach), but the **contractual floor is the $20.25 deal price itself**, backstopped by the ticking fee. The bear *cannot* be modeled below ~$13 without a specific, cited termination event — and even then, a re-shop/bid-reflexivity floor applies.

---

## SECTION 4.5 — Time Horizon Arbitrage

- **Market-implied horizon:** ~3–9 months (T0 Sept-2026 → expected close H1-2027; outside date Aug-2027, extendable Nov-2027). The 2% spread is the market's price for that carry + ~4% break risk.
- **Fundamental compounding horizon (standalone, if the deal broke):** 3–5 years of EWP/fee-EBITDA compounding (20–25% growth, NRR >100%). But this horizon is **moot while the deal is live** — you are paid the contract, not the compound.
- **Arbitrage read:** You are **long a ~6-month, ~95%-probability, +2% carry** with a **5% / −35% tail**. The "horizon arbitrage" is that the market prices the break risk at ~4% while the structural features (no financing condition, 82% pre-commit, ticking fee, top-tier buyer) support a ~5% or lower true break rate — a **thin but positive edge**. There is **no multi-year compounding capture** in this position; do not underwrite it as a compounder.

---

## SECTION 5 — Conviction & Positioning (15-point rubric)

| Pillar | Score | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Quality (business) | 2 / 3 | Genuinely high-quality data/network/annuity business, but active related-party governance overhang |
| Valuation | 1 / 3 | MoS to expected IV ≈ +0.5% (fairly-priced); the 2% spread is thin |
| Macro | 2 / 3 | Deal is macro/credit-decoupled (financing-free); only a systemic sponsor-balance-sheet shock matters |
| Thesis Clarity | 3 / 3 | Binary and transparent: close → $20.25; break → ~$13 |
| Execution | 3 / 3 | Top-tier, equity-committed buyer; no financing condition; 82% pre-commit; unanimous board; ticking fee removes seller walk-incentive |
| **Total** | **11 / 15** | **High conviction tier** |

**Conviction (reported): 10.5 / 15** (High tier; trimmed 0.5 for the unconfirmed regulatory overhang and the thin asymmetry).

**Conviction Decay schedule:** −1 pt per 6 months **unless** a positive completion milestone is hit (regulatory clearance, shareholder vote passed, closing date set). A negative regulatory development is an **immediate** re-underwrite (not a scheduled decay).

**Sizing tier:** **High (5–8%)** — consistent with quarter-Kelly below.

---

## SECTION 5.5 — Behavioral & Positioning

- **Structure:** Post-announcement, ARX trades as a **merger-arb / special-situation** name, not a growth name. The float is thin (82% insider block), so idiosyncratic volume/short squeezes are possible but the price is **anchored to the contract** — it cannot run far above $20.25 (no rational holder sells the deal for more) and is floored by the ticking-fee + re-shop dynamics.
- **Short interest / days-to-cover:** [Unconfirmed — not in pack; not material to a contract-anchored trade]. The relevant "short" is the **deal-break bet**, which is a small, rational minority position, not a crowded short.
- **Institutional crowding score: 3 / 15** (low). Merger-arb books are specialized; this is not a crowded retail momentum name. Low crowding = fewer forced-unwind gaps, supporting orderly exit at the contract.
- **Options skew:** [Unconfirmed]. In a deal, options are typically quoted off the spread; not a decision input.
- **Contrarian sentiment check:** The "bear" narrative (DoI probe, Lloyd's concerns, related-party structure) is **real but priced** — it is precisely why the pre-deal stock was at $13.59 and why the deal carries a ticking fee. The sentiment is not a hidden risk; it is the known, disclosed, contractually-mitigated overhang.

---

## SECTION 6 — Portfolio Fit & Role

- **Role in fund ledger:** **Special-situation / merger-arbitrage carry sleeve.** It is a **low-beta, event-driven, near-riskless (95%) income position**, not a growth compounder. It belongs in the **arbitrage/event sleeve**, sized by Kelly, **not** in the core equity-growth book.
- **Correlation risks:** Near-zero correlation to the equity risk factor while the deal is live (financing-free cash contract). Residual correlations: (i) to **PE-sponsor credit stress** (systemic tail), (ii) to **insurance-regulatory headlines** (idiosyncratic, the main risk).
- **Portfolio risk budgeting:** Allocate from the **event-driven risk budget**, capped at the High-tier 5–8%. The 5% / −35% tail means a 7% position contributes ~1.2% of portfolio NAV to the tail — acceptable within an event sleeve, **not** within a capital-preservation core.

---

## SECTION 6.5 — Mathematical Kelly Sizing

Inputs: T0 = $19.835; Base $20.25 (80%); Bull $20.55 (15%); Bear $13.00 (5%). p (Base+Bull) = 0.95, q (Bear) = 0.05.

- **Payoff ratio (charter, Bull-based):** b = (Bull − T0)/(T0 − Bear) = (20.55 − 19.835)/(19.835 − 13.00) = 0.715 / 6.835 = **0.1046**.
- **Full Kelly (Bull-based):** f* = (p·b − q)/b = (0.95×0.1046 − 0.05)/0.1046 = (0.0994 − 0.05)/0.1046 = **0.472 → 47.2%**.
- **Conservative Kelly (expected-upside-based):** Expected upside = 0.95 × avg-win($0.55) = $0.5225; b_exp = 0.5225/6.835 = 0.0764; f* = (0.95×0.0764 − 0.05)/0.0764 = **0.296 → 29.6%**.
- **Quarter-Kelly (conservative, capital-preserving):** 29.6% / 4 = **7.4%**. (Bull-based quarter-Kelly would be 11.8%; I take the **lower**, expected-upside figure to respect parameter uncertainty in the thin-spread payoff.)
- **Reconcile with conviction cap:** High tier = 5–8%. **7.4% fits.** 

**Recommended ledger allocation weight: 7.0%.**

> **Honesty note:** The payoff ratio (b ≈ 0.10) is poor — you risk ~$1 to win ~$0.10. The edge is **entirely probability-driven** (95% completion), not payoff-driven. This is a **carry trade**, and it is sized small accordingly. It is **not** an asymmetric compounder; do not scale it up on the strength of the underlying business quality.

---

## SECTION 7 — Risks & Institutional Pre-Mortem

**Core risks:**
1. **Insurance-regulatory rejection (the live risk):** A definitive adverse DoI determination on the related-party structure (Hadron fronting ~60% of 3rd-party premium; Augment Risk brokerage) could block or force restructuring of the deal. [Unconfirmed investigation — the USA Herald report states it "has not been publicly confirmed by any agency."]
2. **Deal termination → standalone reversion:** Stock falls to ~$13 (−35%). Mitigant: re-shop/bid-reflexivity floor.
3. **Regulatory delay (not block):** Consumes time; the ticking fee protects the seller but caps the buyer's (and thus the market's) upside — a *slow* deal is a *flat* trade.
4. **Systemic PE-sponsor credit stress:** Low probability; Thoma Bravo is equity-committed with $172B AUM.
5. **Data/governance surprise in the 13E-3 / proxy:** A newly disclosed related-party economics leak could re-rate the standalone down.

**5-year failure pre-mortem ("We lost 50% of the capital allocated to ARX — what went wrong?"):**
The deal **broke** on a **definitive insurance-regulatory finding** that the Altamont-linked fronting/brokerage structure extracted non-arm's-length economics, and the finding was severe enough that (a) Thoma Bravo invoked the termination right and (b) no superior bid emerged because the governance defect was structural, not pricing. The stock reverted to a **deeply governance-discounted standalone (~$10–11, below our $13 bear)** and the thin float amplified the drop. **Lesson embedded in sizing:** the 5% tail is the whole story; we sized at 7% (quarter-Kelly, High cap) precisely so a full bear realization costs the portfolio ~1.2% of NAV, not 50% of a large position. **The pre-mortem is defused by position size and by the hard stop (Section 12 trigger), not by optimism.**

**Tail risk assessment:** The tail is **bounded and known** (contract-anchored, financing-free). It is a **5% / −35%** event, not a fat-tailed blowup. There is no leverage, no margin, no counterparty-default spiral. The tail is **manageable via size and stop.**

---

## SECTION 7.5 — Correlation Risk

- **Stress-period correlation convergence:** In a systemic credit event, PE-sponsor-led deals can see financing re-pricing — but this deal has **no financing condition**, so it is **structurally insulated** from the primary stress channel. Residual convergence is to **insurance-regulatory risk** (idiosyncratic, non-correlated to equity beta).
- **Conditional tail risk:** Conditional on a negative regulatory headline, the stock can gap to ~$13–14 **in one session** (thin float). This is a **gap risk, not a slide** — you cannot always exit at the stop. Hence the position is sized so a full gap-to-bear is a tolerable portfolio event (~1.2% NAV), and the starter tranche is deliberately small (Section 12).

---

## SECTION 8 — Monitoring Milestones & Leading Indicators (M1–M6)

| # | Milestone / KPI | Threshold / Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| **M1** | Proxy / Schedule 13E-3 filed; confirm no new related-party red flags | Any undisclosed related-party economics → re-underwrite immediately |
| **M2** | Shareholder vote | Pass expected (>82% pre-commit). A vote delay or <90% pass → raise break prob to 10%, cut size 50% |
| **M3** | Insurance regulatory clearance (DOIs in key jurisdictions) | Clearance = de-risk to ~98%, allow add to 8%. Adverse finding = **STOP / exit** |
| **M4** | Ticking-fee start date & accrual | If ticking begins, reprice base→bull ($20.25→$20.55); confirms delay, not block |
| **M5** | Outside date (Aug 13, 2027; extendable Nov 13, 2027) | If only regulatory remains at outside date, extension likely → hold; if non-regulatory condition unmet → break risk spikes |
| **M6** | Q3-26 / Q4-26 standalone operating print (EWP, 3rd-party %, fee EBITDA) | EWP growth <10% or 3rd-party penetration decline → standalone (bear) floor softens to ~$12; tighten stop |

**KPI tracking thresholds:** EWP YoY ≥ 15%; 3rd-party % ≥ 40%; fee EBITDA margin ≥ 28%; no adverse regulatory headline. Breach of any → re-underwrite.

---

## SECTION 9 — Adversarial Red Team (5-bullet short thesis)

1. **The related-party structure is the poison pill.** Hadron (Altamont fronting, ~60% of 3rd-party premium) + Augment Risk (Altamont brokerage) + 82% Altamont control = a structure a DoI can find non-arm's-length; a finding blocks the deal *and* impairs the standalone.
2. **Lloyd's already blinked.** Reported "alignment of interest" scrutiny on a prior syndicate attempt is a leading indicator that sophisticated regulators see the governance defect.
3. **The "fee annuity" is circular.** A large share of EWP is placed with sponsor-linked capital; if the 3rd-party penetration is inflated by the ecosystem, the "capital-light" margin story is overstated and the standalone is worth less than $13.
4. **The spread is too thin for the tail.** 2% to make, 35% to lose; even at 95% completion the edge is a rounding error after the unconfirmed regulatory risk — a rational arbitrageur is flat.
5. **Thin float = gap risk.** An 82% insider block means a deal-break headline gaps the stock to $13 with no liquidity to exit at the stop.

**Long vs. Short logic combat scoring:**
- **Long (completion) wins on:** no financing condition (kills #1 break cause), 82% pre-commit (kills vote risk), unanimous board + special-committee process (Morgan Stanley/Houlihan), ticking fee (removes seller walk-incentive), top-tier equity-committed buyer, deal price **above** governance-discounted standalone (rational to close), market-implied ~96% completion.
- **Short (break) wins on:** the unconfirmed but real regulatory overhang, Lloyd's precedent, thin-float gap risk, and the genuinely thin payoff ratio.
- **Killed counter-arguments:** (a) "Financing could fail" — **killed**, no financing condition. (b) "Shareholders could reject" — **killed**, 82% pre-committed. (c) "The business is a fraud" — **killed**, the one-time GAAP loss is a disclosed, equity-neutral IPO accounting charge; adjusted EBITDA is real and cash-backed (OCF positive, NRR >100%). (d) "Standalone is worth $20+" — **killed**, the 49% premium + governance discount means standalone is ~$13–16, *below* the deal.

**Net:** The short thesis is **real but priced and contractually mitigated**. The long (completion) is the **modal, structurally-favored** outcome. Long wins on structure; the short's only live card is a hard regulatory rejection, which is why we carry a 5% tail and a hard stop.

---

## SECTION 10 — Audit Results

**Data freshness tiers:** Deal terms = Tier 1 (Aug 13, 2026); Q2-26 results = Tier 1 (Aug 13, 2026); T0 = Tier 2 (Sept 10, 2026); regulatory = Tier 4 [Unconfirmed].

**Model confidence rating: HIGH on completion probability; MODERATE on the exact bear floor and ticking-fee magnitude** (both bounded and stop-protected).

---

## SECTION 11 — Decision Journal Entry

- **Timestamp / T0:** 2026-09-10; **T0 = $19.835.**
- **Deal:** $20.25 cash, Thoma Bravo, financing-free, close H1-2027, outside Aug 13 2027 (→ Nov 13 2027 if regulatory-only), 6% p.a. ticking on regulatory delay, 82% pre-commit.

- **Scheduled review:** **Monthly**, and **immediately** on any of: proxy/13E-3 filing, shareholder vote, regulatory clearance/adverse finding, ticking-fee trigger, outside-date approach, or a deal-specific price move below $18.00.

---

## SECTION 12 — Final Execution Opinion & Machine Contract

**Final Action: ACCUMULATE (small, event-driven, High-conviction carry).**
This is a **merger-arbitrage position**, not a fundamental buy. The contract is financing-free, 82% pre-committed, board-approved, and priced above the governance-discounted standalone — completion is the modal (~95%) outcome. But the spread is only ~2% against a 5% / −35% tail, so the edge is **probability-driven and thin**. We **accumulate a small starter now** to capture the carry, **add only on a benign wide-spread pullback**, and **hard-stop on any deal-break signal.** It is sized at quarter-Kelly within the High-conviction cap, from the **event-driven risk budget**, not the core growth book.

---

## SECTION 1. Macro Context & Regime Alignment

| Anchor | Value | Source |

The one macro channel is the **opportunity-cost hurdle**: at a 4.83% risk-free rate, a ~2% annualized deal-arb carry fails the hurdle. Credit conditions matter only insofar as they could impair Thoma Bravo's equity commitment (de minimis — TB is a $172B-AUM, well-capitalized buyer with a signed equity commitment and no financing condition).

---

## SECTION 1.5. Historical Base Rates

- **All-cash take-privates with no financing condition + committed controlling seller:** historical break rate ≈ 3–5%. The 22-jurisdiction insurance change-of-control surface and ~9-month window justify a modest uplift → **6% break probability** used here [Assumption, grounded in deal-structure base rates].
- **Broken-deal reversion:** empirically ~60–80% of offer price. Adjusted upward here because a break removes the controlled-company overhang and the business is genuinely growing → bear set at ~74% of deal ($15.00) [Assumption].
- **Insurtech/MGA platform EBITDA multiples (reflation regime):** ~8–12x on normalized adjusted EBITDA [Estimate, peer cross-check].

**Model deviation justification:** I deviate from a pure standalone DCF as the primary lens because a binding, well-capitalized, no-financing-condition offer at a 49% premium dominates standalone value for a ~9-month horizon. ## SECTION 2. Business Quality & Competitive Moat

**Business in 3 sentences:** Accelerant operates the Accelerant Risk Exchange, a data-driven marketplace that connects specialty-insurance underwriters/MGAs with risk-capital providers, charging fees on the Exchange Written Premium transacted through the platform. **7-Factor Moat Scoring (0–3 each):**

| Data/AI switching costs | 2 | Proprietary risk-pricing data; erodes over time, partially replicable |
| Scale/cost advantage | 2 | $4.19B EWP, 22 countries, 600+ products; operating leverage visible |
| Intangible assets/regulation | 1 | Insurance licenses are a barrier but not unique; related-party structure is a governance question mark |

| Counter-positioning (incumbents) | 1 | Lloyd's/MGA incumbents can replicate; "speed" is the only durable edge cited |

**Lynch Classification:** Special (turnaround-to-growth; deal-arb overlay).
**Financial Strength scorecard:** Cash $1.799B vs LT debt $0.121B (net cash ~$1.68B, partly insurance-committed) [Actual]; FY2025 OCF $445M [Actual]; equity $0.698B, retained earnings −$1.537B (GAAP) [Actual]. ---

## SECTION 2.5. Adjusted Financials & Lifecycle Economics

**Forensic reconciliation (the critical one):** The TTM net income of **−$1.357B** (pack, through 2026-03-31) is dominated by the **Q3 2025 one-time, non-cash, equity-neutral profits-interest distribution expense** [Actual — company release]. This is an accounting artifact of the sponsor structure, **not** operating cash burn. Stripping it out:

**Complete Value Cycle / installed-base annuity runway:** The 280-member base at **126% NRR** is the locked-in annuity. Each member's premium book compounds; third-party penetration (now 41% of EWP) converts self-underwriting risk into pure fee income with no balance-sheet risk. The "capacity lock-in" analog is the multi-year MGA/insurer relationships and the data network — these secure the high-margin recurring fee stream the charter requires us to credit.

**Normalized Owner Earnings (FY2026E):**

## SECTION 3. Valuation Synthesis & Triangulation

**WACC derivation:**
- Rf = 4.83% [Actual]
- Beta = 1.1 [Assumption — not available in pack]

**Key triangulation finding:** **The deal price ($20.25) is at the low end of, and slightly below, independent standalone value ($18–24 band, DCF $21.45).** The 49% premium was applied to a *depressed* pre-deal price ($13.61 on 2026-08-12) that reflected the controlled-company overhang, GAAP-loss optics, and sponsor lock-in — not the business's standalone worth. ---

## SECTION 3.5. Second-Order Effects & Reflexivity

- **Competitive counter-moves:** Post-close, Thoma Bravo (a serial insurtech consolidator) will likely bolt on MGAs/data assets, deepening the moat — but this benefits the *private* entity, not public shareholders. No public-market reflexive upside.

- **Balance-sheet reflexivity:** The 6% ticking fee (accrues if close is delayed by *insurance regulatory* approvals) aligns buyer/seller to push approvals through — a reflexive *pro*-completion mechanism. The $136.5M company termination fee (3.2% of equity) and $295.8M parent termination fee (6.4%) are standard and deter a cheap walk-away by either side.

---

## SECTION 4. Scenarios & Bounded Distributions

Causal stress-testing: the "shock" here is **deal non-completion**, transmitted through (i) insurance change-of-control approvals across 22 jurisdictions, (ii) Thoma Bravo strategic re-evaluation, (iii) a topping bid. The contracted-visibility floor applies to the *business* (280-member, 126%-NRR annuity), which supports the $15.00 bear floor even on a break.

| Case | Driver | Intrinsic Value | Prob. |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Base** | Deal closes H1 2027 at contracted $20.25 | **$20.25** | 72% |
| **Bull** | Close + ~2 qtrs of 6% ticking (regulatory delay) + ~15% topping-bid probability | **$20.85** | 22% |

**Confidence Intervals:** 50% CI = $20.25–$20.85 (deal completes, ±ticking); 80% CI = $15.00–$20.85 (includes the 6% break tail).

**MoS vs T0 ($19.835):** +1.2%. **Expected holding-period return:** (20.07−19.835)/19.835 = +1.18% over an expected ~7.5-month close → **≈1.9% annualized**.

## SECTION 4.5. Time Horizon Arbitrage

- **Market-implied horizon:** ~4–9 months (H1 2027 close); the stock already trades at 98% of deal, so the market is holding to close.
- **Fundamental compounding horizon:** 3–5 years (the 126%-NRR annuity compounds to the $21.45 DCF value and beyond).
- **Arbitrage read:** The *fundamental* value ($21.45) is above the deal price, but the *contractual* value ($20.25) caps the public shareholder's realization for ~9 months. You are paid ~2% annualized to wait for the higher fundamental value to be captured by the *private* buyer. **No horizon arbitrage in favor of the public holder** — the compounding accrues to Thoma Bravo post-close.

---

## SECTION 5. Conviction & Positioning

**15-Point Conviction Rubric (0–3 each):**

| Pillar | Score | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Quality | 2 | Genuine growth/moat, but GAAP-loss history, insurance complexity, governance questions |
| Valuation | 1 | Deal price fair; **no margin of safety (1.2%)**; below-hurdle expected return |
| Macro | 2 | Reflation, no headwind; but 4.83% Rf raises the hurdle |
| Thesis Clarity | 3 | Binary, well-defined catalyst (deal close); terms fully verified |

**Conviction Decay:** −1 pt per 6 months if the close slips past H1 2027 without ticking accrual (regulatory drag raises break risk and destroys carry).
**Sizing Tier (mechanical, 9/15 = Medium):** 2–5%. **Reconciled size: 0%** — the below-hurdle expected return and absence of margin of safety override the mechanical tier (see Section 6.5).

---

## SECTION 5.5. Behavioral & Positioning

- **Short interest / days-to-cover:** Not held in pack [Unconfirmed]. In a deal at 98% of price, short interest is typically negligible (limited upside to short, defined catalyst).
- **Institutional crowding (0–15):** ~12/15 — deal-arb desks and momentum flows are heavily positioned long into the close; the 2% spread is the residual after crowding.
- **Options skew:** Not held [Unconfirmed]; expect tight, cheap puts (defined downside to break) and expensive calls (capped upside).
- **Contrarian sentiment check:** The crowd is long the close. There is no contrarian edge at T0; the only edge would be a *pullback* that widens the spread (see tranches).

---

## SECTION 6. Portfolio Fit & Role

- **Asset role:** Short-duration (≤9 mo), defined-catalyst, low-beta deal-arb carry. Not a compounder slot.
- **Correlation risks:** High correlation to (a) insurance-regulatory news flow, (b) Thoma Bravo credit/strategic headlines, (c) general M&A-completion sentiment. Low correlation to equity beta.

## SECTION 6.5. Mathematical Kelly Sizing

- **p** (Base+Bull, deal completes) = 0.94; **q** (Bear, break) = 0.06
- **Payoff ratio b** = (Bull IV − T0)/(T0 − Bear IV) = (20.85 − 19.835)/(19.835 − 15.00) = 1.015/4.835 = **0.210**
- **Full Kelly f\*** = (p·b − q)/b = (0.94×0.210 − 0.06)/0.210 = (0.1974 − 0.06)/0.210 = **0.654 (65.4%)**
- **Quarter-Kelly f\*/4** = **16.4%**

**Reconciliation (the decisive step):** Mathematical quarter-Kelly (16.4%) assumes the payoff is worth taking at the given probabilities. It is **not**, because the **expected annualized return (~1.9%) is below the 4.83% risk-free rate** and there is **no margin of safety**. Kelly sizes *edge*; there is no positive risk-adjusted edge here — the 2% spread is the market's break-risk premium, already paid for. **Recommended ledger allocation weight: 0% (Avoid for new capital).** Existing holders should hold to close (94% probability of $20.25 beats selling at $19.835) but not add.

---

## SECTION 7. Risks & Institutional Pre-Mortem

**Core risks:**
1. **Insurance regulatory change-of-control denial/delay** across 22 jurisdictions (the named ticking-fee trigger) — the primary break/delay risk.
2. **Thoma Bravo strategic re-evaluation** / walk (mitigated by no-financing-condition + $295.8M parent termination fee).
3. **Related-party architecture investigation** (Department of Insurance reportedly examining conflicts/affiliated ties) [Unconfirmed — secondary source]; a negative finding could complicate approvals.
4. **CFO transition** (Green → Huber, effective 2026-03-31) — execution continuity into close.
5. **GAAP/earnings-quality optics** if standalone is ever re-traded.

**5-Year Failure Pre-Mortem ("We lost 50% of capital in 5 years — what went wrong?"):** We initiated at T0 for a ~2% annualized carry; the deal closed on schedule at $20.25 (a ~2% gain), but the *opportunity cost* of locked capital vs. the 4.83% risk-free rate, compounded over the 9-month hold and subsequent redeployment lag, plus a subsequent standalone de-rating if we had rolled into the private-to-public cycle, eroded the position. The failure was not the deal — it was **paying a below-hurdle yield for a high-probability, low-payoff event and mislabeling it as "asymmetric."** The true tail: a regulatory denial (6%) delivering −24% in a single print.

**Tail risk assessment:** Bounded and defined. Maximum loss ≈ −24% (break to $15.00) at 6% probability; no leverage, no financing-condition gap risk, no counterparty credit event of consequence.

---

## SECTION 7.5. Correlation Risk

In a stress period (credit spread widening + insurance-regulatory crackdown), deal-completion correlation converges to 1 with the M&A-arb complex and to negative with risk assets. Conditional tail: a systemic insurance-solvency scare would simultaneously (a) raise break probability and (b) depress the standalone reversion value — a double hit that the 6% point estimate understates in a correlated tail. This is the argument for **0% weight** rather than the mechanical 16.4%.

---

## SECTION 8. Monitoring Milestones & Leading Indicators

| # | Milestone / KPI | Threshold / Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | HSR/antitrust clearance | No second request (expected; no horizontal overlap) |
| M2 | First state DOI change-of-control approvals | ≥50% of jurisdictions approved by Q4 2026 |
| M3 | Ticking-fee trigger | Any regulatory-delay notice → confirms 6% accrual (supports bull case) |
| M4 | Shareholder vote | Altamont 82% vote + majority pass (formality; watch for any dissent) |

## SECTION 9. Adversarial Red Team

**5-bullet institutional short/avoid thesis:**
1. **Below-hurdle carry:** ~1.9% annualized expected return vs. 4.83% risk-free — you are paid less than a Treasury for 9 months of locked, event-risk capital.
2. **No margin of safety:** T0 at 98% of deal; the 2% spread is the break-risk premium, already fully priced. Zero embedded edge.
3. **22-jurisdiction regulatory surface + reported related-party DOI investigation** creates a real, non-diversifiable break/delay tail (6%, −24%).
4. **Negatively skewed payoff:** b = 0.21 — you risk $1 to gain $0.21. This is the *opposite* of the asymmetric profile the charter demands.
5. **Crowding:** Deal-arb desks are fully long; any regulatory wobble triggers a correlated, fast de-rating with no fundamental bid until the break is confirmed.

**Long vs. Short combat scoring:** Long (close) wins on probability (94%) but loses on payoff and hurdle; Short (break) wins on payoff in the tail but is a 6% event and hard to express cleanly. **Net: the long is a fair, unattractive trade; the short is a low-probability tail. Neither clears the institutional bar at T0.**

**Killed counter-arguments:**
- *"It's free money, 94% certain."* — Killed: 94% certain × 2% payoff, below risk-free, with a −24% tail is not free money; it's a thin, crowded carry.
- *"Standalone is worth $21+, so a break isn't bad."* — Partially valid (it caps the bear), but a *break* implies a negative catalyst that the $15.00 floor already discounts; you cannot underwrite the upside of a broken deal as if it were a clean re-rating.
- *"Ticking fee protects the delay."* — Killed: ticking only accrues on *regulatory* delay and for a *capped, unspecified* period [Unconfirmed]; it does not compensate for a break, and the base case (on-schedule close) earns no ticking at all.
